source_meta._title: Console spam: Skipping update for removed player

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.18, using a clean dedicated server and a matching 1.18 client. Run one connected player while retaining direct access to the dedicated-server console and latest.log. Use server view-distance 16. The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, game mode, or required network impairment; use a fresh default Survival world and a local or otherwise high-speed connection as practical controls.
preconditions: The dedicated server and client must both run exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.18, the first version listed as affected.
Use an isolated server directory so settings and logs from another server do not interfere with the reproduction.
The server operator must be able to edit eula.txt and server.properties, start and stop the server, enter commands in the server console, and watch its live log output.
At least one valid Java Edition player account must be able to connect to the server. No in-game operator permission is required because the trigger command is issued from the server console.
Use a fresh default world when practical so the player can move into terrain that has not already been loaded. No seed or coordinates are specified in the report.
Do not artificially throttle the connection for the primary attempt. One comment associated the issue with a slow connection, but another explicitly confirmed it on high-speed connections.
Do not reduce view-distance to 6; the report states that reducing it from 24 to 6 stopped the issue for one reporter.

steps.action: Place the official Minecraft Java Edition 1.18 dedicated-server executable JAR in the isolated server directory. Confirm that the executable is for release 1.18, not 1.18.1 or a later version.
steps.success_cue: The isolated directory contains the Java Edition 1.18 server JAR that will be used for this run.

steps.action: Launch the dedicated server once using a Java runtime capable of running the 1.18 server. Allow it to create its initial configuration files. If it stops because the EULA has not been accepted, leave it stopped.
steps.success_cue: The server directory contains eula.txt and server.properties; the server process is stopped before either file is edited.

steps.action: Open eula.txt in a plain-text editor. After reviewing the EULA, change the EULA property to the acceptance value and save the file. Do not add spaces or additional copies of the property.
steps.success_cue: eula.txt contains one active line reading eula=true.

steps.action: Open server.properties while the server is stopped. Locate the view-distance property, set it to 16, ensure only one active view-distance line remains, and save the file. Leave simulation-distance and all other properties at their generated defaults because the report does not specify changes to them.
steps.success_cue: server.properties is saved with one active view-distance=16 line.

steps.action: Start the Java Edition 1.18 dedicated server again and keep its console visible. Wait for world preparation to finish; do not connect the client while the console still reports spawn preparation or initial world generation.
steps.success_cue: The console has printed the server-ready message beginning with “Done”, and the server accepts connections.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using a client installation configured for exact release 1.18. From the main menu, open Options -> Video Settings and set the client Render Distance to at least 16 chunks so the client does not request less terrain than the server's configured view-distance. Apply the setting and return to the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The running client identifies itself as version 1.18 and its Render Distance is at least 16 chunks.

steps.action: Open Multiplayer, add or directly connect to the dedicated server, and join with exactly one player for the initial attempt. If the client and server are on the same computer, use localhost; otherwise enter the server's actual address.
steps.success_cue: The player is present in the server world, and the server console has logged that the player's login and join completed.

steps.action: Do not begin the trigger sequence immediately after joining. Wait until the terrain around the player has rendered, the loading overlay is gone, movement responds normally, and the server console is no longer reporting initial login or world-loading work.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a fully rendered area and remains connected to the server.

steps.action: Keep the live server console or the live tail of logs/latest.log visible beside the client. Note the current final log line or timestamp so messages generated after the trigger can be separated from earlier startup output.
steps.success_cue: The client remains connected while new server log lines can be observed in real time.

steps.action: On the client, face away from the initially explored area and move continuously toward terrain that has not previously been visited in this fresh world. Use the Move Forward control, default W, and use Sprint, default Left Ctrl, when terrain permits. Avoid pausing the game or disconnecting.
steps.exact_input: Hold W; hold Left Ctrl while sprinting is possible
steps.success_cue: New terrain is repeatedly appearing at the edge of the player's view while the player remains connected and moving.

steps.action: Continue moving until chunks are visibly still being streamed or generated around the outer edge of the 16-chunk view. While this chunk-loading activity is still occurring, leave the client connected and immediately switch control to the dedicated-server console without stopping the server.
steps.success_cue: The player is connected in or beside newly loaded terrain, and the server console is ready to receive a command while chunk updates may still be pending.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, enter the kill command targeting all online players and press Enter. Because this is the server console, enter the command without a leading slash. There should be exactly one connected player, so only the test player is targeted. Execute this only once; repeated kills are unnecessary.
steps.success_cue: The console confirms that one player was killed, and the connected client reaches its death screen or equivalent dead-player state.

steps.action: Do not press Respawn, do not reconnect, do not issue another kill command, and do not stop the server. Immediately transfer control to the observation subsystem while both the client death screen and live server console remain available.
steps.success_cue: The player has just been killed during or immediately after active chunk streaming, remains in the resulting dead-player state, and the server log is still updating live.

stor.handoff_condition: The sole connected player has just been killed from the dedicated-server console while using server view-distance 16 after moving into newly loaded terrain. The client remains on the resulting death screen, no respawn or disconnect action has been taken, and the live server console is visible for immediate observation.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal setup or Steps to Reproduce and does not explicitly identify the player action that starts the console messages.

Using player death as the trigger is reconstructed from every supplied log example showing the affected player entity with removed=KILLED. The report does not state whether the players died naturally, were killed by a command, or reached this state through another sequence.
The kill @a console command is a deterministic practical substitute for the unspecified way the reported players entered the KILLED removal state; it was not supplied by the report.

Moving into unvisited terrain immediately before killing the player is a practical inference intended to create pending player/chunk updates. It is based on comments associating the issue with high server view-distance and, in one case, connection speed, but the report does not explicitly state that movement or new chunk generation is required.

The report provides evidence from dedicated servers and server.properties settings, so this plan uses a dedicated server. It does not conclusively establish that an integrated single-player server cannot exhibit the issue.
The report gives examples at unrelated coordinates and in differently named worlds, so no specific seed, dimension, location, or coordinate can be treated as required.

The report does not specify game mode. The plan retains the server's default Survival mode, but the externally verified Java Edition kill command can target a player without requiring the player to be an operator.

Network conditions are inconsistent across comments: one reporter mentioned a slow connection, while another confirmed the issue with high-speed connections. No network throttling is included in the primary plan.

One reporter used view-distance 24 and another confirmed the messages at view-distance 16. The plan selects 16 because it is explicitly confirmed and is less resource-intensive; it does not assert that 16 is the minimum required value.

The issue may be intermittent. The supplied evidence does not provide a guaranteed delay, travel distance, number of pending chunks, or other deterministic threshold, so this single safe trigger attempt may not reproduce the console output.

Web verification was limited to allowed Minecraft sources and was used only to confirm that view-distance is a server.properties option in Java Edition 1.18 and that the Java Edition kill command accepts an entity selector such as @a. It did not reveal an official missing reproduction procedure for MC-243489.

source_meta._title: The game output console is logged with errors regarding missing signatures from property textures when joining LAN worlds

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w24a using two simultaneously running clients on the same local network. One client hosts an ordinary singleplayer world through the integrated server's Open to LAN feature; the second client joins that LAN world. Use two distinct authenticated Minecraft accounts. This is not a dedicated-server reproduction. The joining client's external Minecraft Launcher Game Output window must be open so its output can be captured during connection.
preconditions: Two computers, or equivalent isolated client environments, can run Minecraft: Java Edition simultaneously and communicate over the same local network.
The host client and joining client are signed in with two different authenticated Minecraft accounts; using the same account for both clients may prevent simultaneous play.
Both clients have an unmodified snapshot 22w24a installation available and selected.
Local firewall and network settings permit Minecraft LAN discovery and connections between the two clients.
The joining player's Minecraft Launcher is configured to open the external Game Output window when Java Edition starts.
Do not substitute an ordinary singleplayer-only session or a dedicated multiplayer server for the Open to LAN integrated-server session.

steps.action: On the host computer, open Minecraft Launcher and sign in with the first Minecraft account. On the joining computer, open Minecraft Launcher and sign in with a different Minecraft account.
steps.success_cue: The two launchers display different signed-in player profiles and can be used at the same time.

steps.action: On each launcher, open the Java Edition Installations page. Enable display of snapshot versions if necessary, then create or edit an installation whose version is snapshot 22w24a. Save and select that installation on both clients.
steps.success_cue: Both launchers have snapshot 22w24a selected as the installation that will start when Play is pressed.

steps.action: On the joining player's launcher, open Settings, locate the Minecraft: Java Edition settings, and enable the option that opens the output log when the game starts. This Launcher option is documented as "Open the output log when the game starts." ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Launcher?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Open the output log when the game starts
steps.success_cue: The output-log option is enabled for the joining player's launcher.

steps.action: On the host client, launch the selected 22w24a installation and wait for the Minecraft main menu to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: The host is at the Minecraft main menu and the displayed game version is 22w24a.

steps.action: On the host client, click Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Create a disposable test world by clicking Create New World, leaving all settings not specified by the report at their defaults, and clicking Create New World again. If an ordinary test world already exists, it may instead be selected and opened.
steps.success_cue: The host player is inside a singleplayer world, surrounding terrain has rendered, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: On the host client, press Esc to open the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The Game Menu is displayed over the host's world.

steps.action: Click Open to LAN in the host's pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The LAN World configuration screen is displayed, including the Start LAN World button.

steps.action: Do not impose a particular game mode or Allow Cheats value because the report specifies neither. Click Start LAN World using the currently displayed values.
steps.success_cue: The host returns to the world and an in-game confirmation states that the local game was hosted, normally including a dynamically assigned port number.

steps.action: Leave the host client running inside the LAN-opened world. Do not return to the title screen, close the world, or close the host game.
steps.success_cue: The host remains connected to the world and the LAN session remains available to other local clients.

steps.action: On the joining computer, launch the selected 22w24a installation. Confirm that a separate Game Output window opens alongside the game, and leave that window open. If it does not open, close the joining game, re-enable the launcher setting from step 3, and relaunch before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The joining client is at the 22w24a main menu and its external Game Output window is open and receiving startup log lines.

steps.action: On the joining client's main menu, click Multiplayer. If a one-time multiplayer warning screen is shown, acknowledge it using its Proceed button.
steps.success_cue: The joining client is on the Play Multiplayer screen and is scanning the local network for games.

steps.action: Wait without closing the host world until the host's session appears in the joining client's multiplayer list under the LAN-games area.
steps.success_cue: A LAN world entry associated with the host player or hosted world is visible and selectable in the multiplayer list.

steps.action: Keep the joining client's Game Output window open and ensure its contents are being retained or captured. If possible, arrange the game and output windows so the output remains visible during connection; do not evaluate any particular log message yet.
steps.success_cue: The LAN world is visible in the multiplayer list and the joining client's Game Output console is ready to capture the complete connection period.

steps.action: On the joining client, select the host's LAN world entry and click Join Server, or double-click the LAN world entry once. Do not repeatedly activate the entry.
steps.success_cue: The joining client leaves the multiplayer list and begins the connection/world-loading sequence for the host's LAN world.

stor.handoff_condition: The joining player has just activated the host's LAN world entry, connection or terrain loading has begun, and the joining client's Game Output window remains open and is capturing output. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately so it can monitor the console throughout the join and until the world finishes loading.
uncertainties: The report does not specify an operating system, world seed, world game mode, difficulty, Allow Cheats setting, coordinates, graphics settings, resource packs, or a required player skin. This plan leaves those unspecified values at ordinary defaults.

The precise wording and placement of the launcher's output-log option can vary between launcher builds or platforms. The externally verified launcher documentation identifies it under the Minecraft: Java Edition settings as "Open the output log when the game starts."

The report does not supply a direct-connect IP address or port. This plan therefore uses automatic LAN discovery as described by the report; the dynamically assigned port is only known after the host opens the world to LAN.

Later comments mention intermittent occurrences in singleplayer worlds on newer versions, which conflicts with the report description's LAN-only characterization. This plan preserves the formal report's deterministic Open to LAN reproduction and uses the first formally listed affected version.
No repetition count is specified. The plan performs one LAN join so the observation subsystem can inspect that single trigger without intentionally generating repeated log output.

source_meta._title: The server console or LAN game output spammed with "PLAYER moved too quickly!" after a player dies and respawns

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition using the official vanilla 24w37a dedicated server and a client running the matching 24w37a installation. Keep the dedicated server console visible and continuously capturing output. Use one test player with operator permission; do not use a LAN-hosted single-player world, mods, plugins, or the teleport command for this reproduction.
preconditions: The official vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 24w37a dedicated server files are installed, the EULA has been accepted, and the server can start normally.
A Minecraft Java Edition client installation for exactly 24w37a is available.
The server world is not Hardcore, so the player can respawn after death.
Only one test player should be connected, ensuring that the report-supplied @p selector targets that player deterministically.
The test player has operator permission so the report-supplied /kill command can be executed from in-game chat.
The dedicated server console is visible or its live output is otherwise being captured before the player is killed.
The player must not use a bed, respawn anchor, /spawnpoint, or another mechanism to change the respawn point after its location has been recorded.

steps.action: Start the official vanilla 24w37a dedicated server using its normal launch procedure, with the server console kept visible.
steps.success_cue: The server console reports that startup is complete and the server is ready to accept player connections.

steps.action: If the test player is not already an operator, enter the operator command directly in the dedicated server console. Replace the placeholder with the exact Minecraft profile name of the test player. Do not include a leading slash in the server console.
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the test player was made a server operator.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 24w37a on the client, open Multiplayer, connect to the dedicated server, and wait for the world to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The test player is standing in the server world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and no other players are connected.

steps.action: At the player's initial respawn location, press the debug-screen control, F3 by default, and record the displayed X and Z coordinates. Treat this location as the respawn point for measuring the required travel distance. Do not sleep in a bed or otherwise change the respawn point.
steps.success_cue: The respawn point's X and Z coordinates have been recorded while the player remains near that point.

steps.action: Close the debug screen if desired, face a safe horizontal direction, and move away from the recorded respawn point by normal walking or sprinting. Use W to move forward and optionally hold the Sprint action, Left Ctrl by default. Do not use /teleport, /tp, or any other teleportation method.
steps.success_cue: The player has physically traveled away from the respawn point without using a teleport command.

steps.action: Use the F3 debug coordinates to continue traveling until the player's X or Z coordinate is at least 48 blocks from the corresponding recorded coordinate, representing three full chunk widths in one horizontal direction.
steps.success_cue: The player is at least three chunk widths, 48 horizontal blocks, away from the recorded respawn point along X or Z.

steps.action: Stop moving and wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and normal movement and server interaction are responsive. Leave the dedicated server console visible or continuously captured.
steps.success_cue: The destination area is loaded, the player is stationary and responsive, and the server console is ready to capture output from the next actions.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The in-game chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report-supplied command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Execute it from the test player's in-game chat rather than from the server console.
steps.success_cue: The command kills the test player and the death screen appears with a Respawn button.

steps.action: Click the Respawn button once and immediately hand control to the observation subsystem while the dedicated server console continues to be captured.
steps.success_cue: The Respawn button has been activated and the client has begun leaving the death screen or loading the player back at the respawn point.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just clicked Respawn after being killed at least three chunk widths from the recorded respawn point, and the dedicated vanilla server console is actively visible or being captured. Begin observing the console output immediately while the respawn completes.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a world seed, coordinates, game mode, difficulty, operating system, or server.properties configuration; no special values are introduced for them beyond requiring a non-Hardcore world.

The report says to move "3 chunks away" but does not define whether this means chunk-index separation or a precise coordinate distance. The plan conservatively uses at least 48 blocks along X or Z, equal to three full 16-block chunk widths.

The title also mentions LAN game output, but the formal reproduction steps specifically require the official vanilla dedicated server. This plan therefore uses the dedicated-server path and does not substitute a LAN world.

The report does not state how many players were online. Restricting the test to one connected player is a practical choice that makes the supplied @p selector unambiguous without changing the command.
